description: Candidate benchmark and eval sources for deriving reviewed span-level RAMP corpus examples.
safety_note: Do not ingest operational harmful prompts verbatim into the public repo. Extract bounded spans, labels, source IDs, and provenance; store restricted raw examples outside the public repository when necessary.

sources.name: RAMP synthetic non-instructional seed spans
sources.notes: Safe abstract examples used to validate schema before benchmark-derived spans.

sources.name: XSTest
sources.notes: Best source for exaggerated-safety and over-refusal cases because safe prompts are paired with unsafe contrasts.

sources.name: WildGuardMix / WildGuard
sources.notes: Useful for harmful-vs-benign prompt classification and contrastive benign prompts.

sources.name: HarmBench
sources.notes: Use behavior categories and reviewed spans; avoid storing operational details in public artifacts.

sources.name: JailbreakBench
sources.notes: Use attack family, behavior, and judge labels for evasion spans and classifier-targeting metadata.

sources.name: StrongREJECT
sources.notes: Useful for measuring whether jailbreaks elicit specific harmful responses; extract non-operational spans.

sources.name: BeaverTails
sources.notes: Large human-preference safety alignment dataset with helpfulness and harmlessness annotations.

sources.name: SafetyBench
sources.notes: Multiple-choice safety benchmark; better for taxonomy mapping and category coverage than free-form span extraction.

sources.name: SALAD-Bench
sources.notes: Hierarchical safety benchmark useful for checking RAMP taxonomy coverage and attack-enhanced safety categories.

sources.name: Do-Not-Answer
sources.notes: Prompts responsible models should not answer; useful for boundary spans and refusal-label calibration.

sources.name: ToxicChat
sources.notes: Real chat moderation dataset; useful for user-message phrasing and toxicity boundaries.

sources.name: ToxiGen
sources.notes: Useful for implicit hate, group references, and benign statements near toxic semantic space.

sources.name: RealToxicityPrompts
sources.notes: Useful for toxicity scores and continuation-risk spans; not a complete safety taxonomy.

sources.name: CyberSecEval
sources.notes: Cyber-specific source for unsafe assistance, insecure code, and safety-utility tradeoff.

sources.name: WMDP
sources.notes: Use carefully as hazardous-knowledge proxy. Prefer category mapping and restricted-review handling over public span extraction.

sources.name: AgentHarm
sources.notes: Contains harmful/offensive agent prompts and usage restrictions; use only for safety/security research and preserve license constraints.

sources.name: MLCommons AILuminate Demo Prompt Dataset
sources.notes: Useful for aligning RAMP categories with MLCommons hazard categories; keep eval contamination concerns in mind.
